title: Iterative Collection De-duplication (Ignoring Set Types)
pattern: Manually traversing a list and checking for duplicates iteratively instead of leveraging built-in set data structures.
why_bad: High algorithmic complexity. This nested loop approach operates in O(N^2) time, drastically penalizing performance on larger collections compared to O(N) set-based de-duplication.
detection: A loop over a sequence checking for existence in a result container before appending, without using a `HashSet` or standard `dedup()__`.
counterexample: De-duplicating a statically-bounded small array (e.g., 2-3 items) where a HashSet allocation overhead would exceed the O(N^2) search cost.
fix: Convert the collection to a Set or utilize the standard collection's de-duplication traits.
source: *The Art of Readable Code (Foucher & Boswell), Chapter 11, p. 115 [360]*
